title: Benefit Withholding and Deduction Orders on Form 1099-G, with Refund Periods and Recovery Routes
content:
Each kind of Benefit Withholding and Deduction Orders has its own Form 1099-G box for the year's deductions (or none), its own number of business days within which a deduction taken in error is refunded when it has not yet been remitted, and its own route by which the claimant recovers a deduction that has already been remitted.

| Kind | Form 1099-G box for the year's deductions | Business days to refund a deduction taken in error before it was remitted | Where the claimant recovers a deduction already remitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| Voluntary Federal Income Tax Withholding | Box 4 | 10 | As a claim on the claimant's federal income tax return |
| Voluntary State Income Tax Withholding | Box 11 | 10 | As a claim on the claimant's state income tax return |
| Child Support Withholding — Current Support Order | 0 — not reported | 10 | By request to the State Disbursement Unit |
| Child Support Withholding — Arrears-Only Order | 0 — not reported | 10 | By request to the State Disbursement Unit |
| SNAP Overissuance Recovery — Household or Agency Error | 0 — not reported | 10 | By request to the SNAP agency |
| SNAP Overissuance Recovery — Intentional Program Violation | 0 — not reported | 10 | By request to the SNAP agency |

### Form 1099-G

Federal income tax withheld from benefits during the year appears in Box 4 of the claim's Form 1099-G; state income tax withheld appears in Box 11. Deductions under the two child support kinds and the two SNAP Overissuance Recovery kinds are not reported on Form 1099-G (box shown as 0).

### Refund period

The refund period is the same for all six kinds: 10 business days for a deduction taken in error that had not yet been remitted.

### Recovery of a remitted deduction

A deduction that has already been remitted is recovered through the route in the last column, which depends on the payee:

- federal income tax withholding — claimed on the federal income tax return;
- state income tax withholding — claimed on the state income tax return;
- child support deductions — requested from the State Disbursement Unit;
- SNAP Overissuance Recovery deductions — requested from the SNAP agency.

### Matching a box to a kind (hypothetical)

| Amount on a claimant's Form 1099-G | Kind it belongs to |
|---|---|
| A figure in Box 4 | Voluntary Federal Income Tax Withholding |
| A figure in Box 11 | Voluntary State Income Tax Withholding |
| A child support or SNAP Overissuance Recovery deduction | Not shown on Form 1099-G |
